title: grep: find the lines you need
summary: Search a file, or a whole folder, for a word, and the few options you'll use every day.

text: grep prints the lines that contain your word. The file doesn't change.
- Put quotes around a pattern with spaces: grep 'disk full' app.log.
- -v is handy to hide noise: grep -v DEBUG app.log.
- [ ] and . mean something special to grep. -F (or a \ before each) makes them plain: grep -cF '[ERROR]' app.log.
-r searches every file in a folder and below.
- Each line starts with the file and, with -n, the line number.
